children: The dollar will likely trade around 4.07 ringgit next week, with U.S. economic data and U.S.-Iran talks in focus, Kenanga economists say in a note. U.S. August PCE core inflation data and September payrolls are likely to be crucial, with stronger-than-expected data potentially raising expectations for the Fed's further rate increases and supporting the dollar, they say. Kenanga expects the dollar to face resistance at 4.090 ringgit, with support at 4.072 ringgit. The dollar is 0.2% lower at 4.0761 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
